transcript.text: Everyone, I've finished my exam on our stroke alert patient. I have some critical findings that I need to share with the group before we proceed. The clinical picture is concerning for a large-vessel occlusion, and time is brain. Dr. Chen, I think we need to huddle at the bedside as we usually do, but I want to make sure everyone has the key clinical details first.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to share critical medication information before we proceed. I verified that the patient took apixaban 5 mg six hours ago. Because of this active anticoagulation, intravenous alteplase must not be administered under the current medication history.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to share critical imaging information before we finalize our pathway. I confirmed that the patient has a non-MRI-compatible implanted neurostimulator, so MRI cannot be used. However, CT angiography followed by CT perfusion is available immediately and can be completed before transfer.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: Thank you all for these critical updates. Let me summarize what we know before I make my decision. Dr. Alvarez, you've identified this as concerning for a large-vessel occlusion. Nina, thank you — the patient took apixaban 5 mg six hours ago, which means IV alteplase is contraindicated due to active anticoagulation. Dr. Wallace, MRI is off the table due to the implanted neurostimulator, but CT angiography followed by CT perfusion is available immediately. So our pathway is becoming clear: no IV alteplase, proceed with CTA/CTP to evaluate for large-vessel occlusion and guide potential thrombectomy. Let me formalize this decision now.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Thank you, Dr. Chen. To confirm from pharmacy's perspective: IV alteplase is contraindicated due to the confirmed apixaban 5 mg taken six hours ago. I'll be ready to support the thrombectomy pathway from a medication standpoint once CTA/CTP confirms the occlusion. If there are any reversal agent considerations needed before the procedure, I can advise on that as well.
